sentences: It starts with a notification.
A charge you don't recognize.
In three years of this bank's data, forty percent of all complaints were card disputes.
Each one took fifteen days.
One in five missed its deadline.
What if it took a minute?
Meet NiceBank.
Just say it the way you would say it.
NiceBank finds the exact transaction in your own history, and shows it in your currency, in dollars, and at that day's rate.
It acts only when you confirm.
Then it checks that the case really exists, before it tells you it's done.
Not every scary charge is a dispute.
Reversed, pending or declined: NiceBank explains it from your own record, instead of opening a case nobody needs.
And when something is sensitive, like blocking a card, it asks for a second factor, right inside the conversation.
Spanish or Portuguese, it understands.
And no one can talk it into moving money.
It simply can't.
When a person should decide, a specialist gets the whole case: verified facts, actions taken, open questions.
Nobody asks the customer twice.
And their name stays encrypted until the specialist takes the case.
And the customer hears back by email, in their own language, the moment anything changes.
And the bank sees all of it, live: what was resolved, what was escalated, and why.
Under the hood, one rule.
AI proposes. Code decides.
A trained classifier and a language model understand the message.
Deterministic code decides with a versioned policy, acts, verifies, and audits every step.
Go, React, Keycloak, Postgres with row-level security, and OpenTelemetry: built for production, not just for a demo.
And every turn is traced, end to end: each step, each rule, each millisecond.
On a hundred and twenty cases it had never seen, NiceBank got eighty-seven percent right.
Today's process: six.
Zero unsafe outcomes.
Every manipulation attempt, blocked.
And under a second per reply.
NiceBank.
Disputes, settled in a minute.
Try it now at hackathon dot evon dot solutions.
